title: Chapter 10: The Prideful 5
content:
Chapter 10

The Prideful 5

Wei Wuxian rubbed his aching lower back, bracing himself against the spotted donkey as he clambered up from the dirt. Safe behind the beast’s flanks, he practically yowled at the top of his lungs, "Oh, aren't you incredible! Big family, big power, tossing your weight around! Hitting innocent people whenever you feel like it! Tsk, tsk, tsk!"

Lan Wangji stayed dead silent.

Jiang Cheng’s jaw clenched, his mind racing between fury and disbelief. How is this possible?!

Zidian possessed a lethal, absolute trick: if a body-snatcher was struck by its lash, the soul and the stolen vessel were torn apart on impact. The possessing spirit would be ripped clean out of the stolen flesh, without exception. Yet this lunatic had taken a direct hit across the spine and was still jumping around, throwing tantrums like nothing happened. Barring the fact that this body wasn't possessed at all, there was simply no other explanation.

Behind the donkey, Wei Wuxian sneered to himself. Of course Zidian can't whip my soul out, genius. I didn't steal this body—it was handed to me on a silver platter. A forced sacrificial contract!

Seeing the sheer suspicion still darkening Jiang Cheng’s face, his hand itching to loose the whip a second time, Lan Jingyi piped up indignantly, "Sect Leader Jiang, that's enough! That was Zidian!"

Against a spiritual treasure of Zidian’s legendary standing, there was no such thing as failing on the first strike only to work on the second. If it didn't extract a soul, there was no soul to extract; if it didn't reveal a possession, then no possession had occurred. Anything else would mean Zidian was a complete sham. Calling it out like that backed Jiang Cheng straight into a corner, and given how viciously he guarded his own face, he couldn't very well lash out again.

Yet if this wasn't Wei Wuxian, who else in the world could command Wen Ning?!

Jiang Cheng refused to accept it. Leveling his crackling whip straight at the donkey, his voice turned venomously low. "Who the hell are you?!"

One of the nosy cultivators hovering on the sidelines cleared his throat, cautiously chiming in, "Ah, Sect Leader Jiang, you probably wouldn't bother with these kinds of petty rumors, but this Mo Xuanyu fellow... well, he used to be a disciple of the Lanling Jin Sect. An outer member, you know. But because his spiritual roots were weak and his progress stalled—on top of that business where he harassed a fellow male disciple—he was kicked out of Koi Tower in disgrace. Word is he completely lost his mind afterward. If you ask me, he likely turned to the crooked path out of bitter frustration when orthodox methods failed him. It doesn't necessarily mean... the Yiling Laozu stole his body."

Jiang Cheng snapped, "That business? What business?"

"Well... you know, that kind of thing..."

Someone else in the back couldn't resist blurting it out: "He prefers men! A cutsleeve!"

Jiang Cheng’s eyebrow gave a violent twitch, his disgust deepening with every syllable.

A few murmurs remained unspoken, though everyone was thinking them.

Terrible as his reputation was, no one could deny that before he defected from the Jiang Clan, the Yiling Laozu had been a strikingly handsome young gentleman—accomplished in the arts, effortlessly charming, officially ranked fourth among all the eligible young masters in the cultivation world. Coincidentally, this short-tempered Jiang Sect Leader had placed fifth, perpetually stuck in his shadow, which was why nobody dared bring up the old beauty charts to his face. Wei Ying had always been a shameless flirt, chasing pretty maidens and leaving broken hearts in his wake, but no one had ever heard a whisper of him having a taste for men. Even if he were to crawl back from hell... with Wei Ying’s haughty tastes, he would never have stooped to piloting a fruit-munching, donkey-riding, clown-painted lunatic!

Another cultivator muttered under his breath, "Honestly, it doesn't look like him at all... and that flute playing was downright atrocious. Talk about a cheap knockoff."

During the Sunshot Campaign, the Yiling Laozu had stood above the carnage, a lone bamboo flute echoing through the night as he steered armies of the dead to rip through enemy ranks like an unstoppable tide. His melody had been terrifying, majestic art; comparing that legend to the squeaking, dying-pig noises this discarded Jin bastard had just produced was an insult to the dead.

Wei Wuxian felt deeply victimized. You try going thirteen years without practice, hack a whistle out of a raw bamboo stalk with a stolen sword, and see what kind of masterpiece you manage to blow! If you can play anything that sounds remotely decent, I'll get down on my knees and kowtow to you!

A moment ago, Jiang Cheng had been utterly convinced he was staring at his greatest nemesis, his blood boiling hot. But Zidian had clearly delivered its verdict: Not him. The whip never lied, and it never failed. Forcing himself to calm down, Jiang Cheng ran the angles: It doesn't matter. I'll haul him back under any excuse, bleed him dry with every interrogation trick in the book, and see what spills out. He'll slip up eventually. It wasn't as though he hadn't done the exact same thing to countless suspected body-snatchers before.

Having settled on a plan, Jiang Cheng gave a subtle hand signal. Taking the cue, his purple-clad disciples fanned out to encircle the donkey. Wei Wuxian panicked, scrambling straight behind Lan Wangji’s white robes, clutching his chest with theatrical terror. "Ah! What are you trying to do to me?!"

Lan Wangji glanced back at him, enduring the obnoxious, overdramatic display without a word.

Seeing that Lan Wangji had no intention of stepping aside, Jiang Cheng’s voice chilled. "Second Young Master Lan, are you deliberately trying to cross me?"

Everyone in the cultivation world knew the young leader of the Jiang Clan was hopelessly paranoid when it came to Wei Wuxian. He operated on a policy of capturing ten innocent suspects rather than letting a single body-snatcher slip through; anyone who even vaguely resembled Wei Wuxian was hauled back to Lotus Pier for brutal torture. If this lunatic fell into his hands, he’d be lucky to leave with half his skin intact.

Lan Sizhui stepped forward, trying to mediate. "Sect Leader Jiang, the truth is plain to see. Young Master Mo hasn't stolen a body. Why must you torment a harmless, nameless wanderer?"

Jiang Cheng sneered, "Then I wonder why the esteemed Second Young Master Lan has gone out of his way to shield a harmless, nameless wanderer since the moment he arrived?"

A smothered snicker slipped past Wei Wuxian’s lips.

He poked his head out from behind Lan Wangji's back. "Sect Leader Jiang, look... your aggressive flirting is really putting me in an awkward spot."

Jiang Cheng’s brow jumped, a visceral gut instinct warning him that whatever was about to come out of this lunatic's mouth would be catastrophic for his blood pressure.

Wei Wuxian sighed with exaggerated pity. "I appreciate the passion, really, but you’re getting way ahead of yourself. Just because I like men doesn't mean I take anyone with a pulse. I don't just follow any guy who waves a finger at me. And frankly? You’re just not my type."

Wei Wuxian was deliberately gunning to disgust him. If there was one thing Jiang Cheng hated above all else, it was being told he was second best. No matter how absurd the comparison was, the moment someone claimed he fell short of someone else, he’d stew in bitter fury for days, refusing to rest until he proved them wrong.

Sure enough, Jiang Cheng’s face twisted into an ugly, mottled gray. "Oh? Then do enlighten me: what kind is your type?"

Wei Wuxian beamed. "My type? Hmm... Someone like Hanguang-jun. He’s totally my style."

Now, if there was one thing Lan Wangji despised above all else, it was shallow, shameless, frivolous banter. The moment the joke hit his ears, he would naturally recoil and put ten paces of distance between them to protect his pristine dignity.

Grossing out two birds with one stone—pure genius!

Yet, the moment the words left his mouth, Lan Wangji turned around.

His expression remained carved from pure, unreadable stone as he leveled a gaze at Wei Wuxian. "You said it yourself."

Wei Wuxian blinked, his grin freezing. "...Huh?"

Lan Wangji faced Jiang Cheng once more, his posture impeccably courteous, yet carrying an absolute, unyielding finality:

"This man is coming back to Gusu with me."

Wei Wuxian went rigid.

Wait, what?!
